title: Orthogonally invariant macroscopic blocks have dimension-suppressed negative defect

radial_rigidity.law: Let X=RU in R^d be centered, standardized and orthogonally invariant, with U uniform on the unit sphere, E R^2=d and finite E R^4.
radial_rigidity.negative_floor: Jensen E[R^4]>=d^2 gives kappa4(<u,X>)>=-6||u||^4/(d+2), sharply attained by fixed radius.
radial_rigidity.fourier_bound: For one d_N=Theta(N^3) block with bounded covariance profile and bounded trigonometric basis, int||a_N(x)||^4dx=O(N^4), so D_N>=-O(N).
radial_rigidity.coefficient: K1637 yields Q_N>=lambda_N^statG-O(N); the profiled Gaussian is a radial member, so the class coefficient is h_g^prof.
radial_rigidity.scope_guard: The theorem needs orthogonal invariance after standardization and does not control angularly anisotropic macroscopic laws such as K1647.
